posts.body_html:
Some new photos of S. x Elaine, named after my fiance. It will officially be published in the near future once most characteristics of this plant are observed.

So far, it behaves like an S. flava early in the grow season by putting on a nice flush of traps. However, it behaves like an S. leucophylla in late summer and fall. After the spring pitchers, it produces a huge amount of phyllodia, and then has its fall pitcher production. I bet once this plant is big enough, it'll make some nice specimens.

photos taken 9/16/2012-the color has been consistent in the spring and fall pitchers:

posts.body_html:
So this is the first year that S. x Elaine Wang and many of "her" siblings have flowered. Flower colors range from a standard yellow to red, and so far, there's nothing in between. Adrian slack has red flowers (when grown in full sun), and so does S x Judith Hindle, so it's rather interesting that these recessive yellow color genes (from S. flava) came through. It makes sense though-both judith hindle and adrian slack have recessive yellow flower genes in them:



I think these pics were taken 4/13/13:
